properties.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued August 9 at 1:01AM CDT until August 9 at 1:45AM CDT by NWS Aberdeen SD
properties.description:
SVRABR

The National Weather Service in Aberdeen has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northeastern Edmunds County in north central South Dakota...
South Central McPherson County in north central South Dakota...

* Until 145 AM CDT.

* At 101 AM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 5 miles north of
Roscoe, moving southeast at 25 mph.

HAZARD...Ping pong ball size hail and 60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...People and animals outdoors will be injured. Expect hail
damage to roofs, siding, windows, and vehicles. Expect
wind damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* This severe thunderstorm will be near...
Roscoe around 105 AM CDT.
Ipswich around 140 AM CDT.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued August 9 at 12:58AM CDT until August 9 at 1:30AM CDT by NWS Aberdeen SD
properties.description:
At 1258 AM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located near Mound City, or
5 miles southeast of Herreid, moving east at 25 mph.

HAZARD...Two inch hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...People and animals outdoors will be injured. Expect damage
to roofs, siding, windows, and vehicles.

This severe thunderstorm will be near...
Mound City and Herreid around 100 AM CDT.
properties.instruction:
Anyone outdoors should move to shelter inside a well-built structure
and stay away from windows. This storm is capable of producing
dangerous hail.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued August 9 at 1:44AM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
properties.description:
At 144 AM EDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Oak Hill, moving east at 35 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph and pea size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Point Pleasant, Gallipolis, Oak Hill, Rio Grande, Gallia, Cheshire,
Adamsville, Gallopolis Ferry, Mabee, Gage, and Centerpoint.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

Frequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Lightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle.

properties.description:

This includes Route 50 in West Virginia between mile markers 40 and
77.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued August 8 at 10:29PM MST until August 9 at 12:00AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until midnight MST tonight.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1029 PM MST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain due to thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly in the advisory area. Between 0.75 and
2 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.1 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Wickenburg.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued August 8 at 8:13PM CDT until August 9 at 3:35PM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden.

* WHEN...Until Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 14.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding occurs, and causes
sloughs and peripheral channels near the main stream to cut off
areas of the flood plain, isolating livestock and damaging
equipment in low areas. Oil field tank batteries and pump jacks
flood.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM CDT Saturday the stage was 14.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
tonight and fall below action stage by late Monday.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 14.3
feet on 05/24/2004.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.
